name: Le Nguyen Hai Dang
tagline: Backend developer focused on Go and .NET, with a growing interest in DevOps and AI engineering.
bio: I build backend systems and the infrastructure that keeps them observable — services in Go and .NET, backed by Postgres, containers, and a Prometheus/Grafana/Loki monitoring stack. Lately I've been pushing further into DevOps practice and applied AI engineering.

projects.name: Tekticket - A modern ticket ordering and event management platform
projects.description: Backend for an online ticket ordering and event management platform — handles catalog, seat/ticket inventory, checkout, and payment webhooks.
highlights: Payment flow built on Stripe, with webhook handling for order state transitions
Full observability stack wired in: metrics via Prometheus/Grafana, logs via Loki/Promtail
Postgres schema modelling events, seat inventory, and orders under concurrent checkout

projects.name: Serina - A chess engine built purely in Go
projects.description: A chess engine written in Go — bitboard representation, move generation, and search using Minimax and Alpha-Beta pruning.
highlights: Move generation and board state built from scratch, no external chess libraries
Search and evaluation tuned for reasonable play strength within a time budget

projects.name: RespiraAMS - A clinical decision support system for CAP disease
projects.description: A clinical decision support system for empirically diagnosing community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), built for hospital use as a set of .NET microservices.
highlights: First module assesses patient severity and recommended treatment site
Reconciles three overlapping severity scales — CURB-65/CRB-65, the Pneumonia Severity Index, and ATS ICU criteria
Core challenge: the scales share metrics that are transformed differently (CURB-65 uremia vs. ATS BUN) or combined differently (PSI's PaO2 vs. ATS's PaO2/FiO2 ratio), alongside boolean criteria
